title: Interfaces versus abstract classes
context: What do interfaces and abstract classes have in common, and how do they differ?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Both can declare methods that subclasses must implement, and neither can be instantiated. An abstract class can hold state (fields), constructors, and concrete methods. A class can extend only one abstract class. An interface defines a contract. A class can implement many interfaces. Since Java 8 interfaces can have default and static methods, but they still hold no instance state. Use an interface for a capability shared across unrelated classes, and an abstract class for shared base behaviour.

points.title: Single versus multiple inheritance
points.why: A class can extend one abstract class but implement many interfaces.

points.title: State
points.why: Abstract classes can hold fields. Interfaces only have constants.
